```{r g24-tables-setup}
## The colors of the 2024 print tables: the ground, the ink, a light gray rule under every row and the source gray.
g24t_ground <- econ$print$bg$value[1]
g24t_ink <- econ$print$text
g24t_rule <- p24[["light gray"]]
g24t_gray <- econ$print$source

## Fira Sans Condensed is loaded from Google Fonts, so tables use it whether or not it is installed.
g24t_font <- list(gt::google_font("Fira Sans Condensed"), "Roboto Condensed", "Arial Narrow", "sans-serif")

## The print tab (3.4 by 0.45 times the axis-label size), the bold headline and the bold print subtitle, at the
## chart sizes of the main document.
g24t_heading <- function(title, subtitle = NULL) {
  gt::html(paste0(
    sprintf(
      '<div style="width:%gpt;height:%gpt;background:%s;margin:0 0 %gpt 0"></div>',
      3.4 * g24_size, 0.45 * g24_size, accent24[["print"]], 1.2 * g24_size
    ),
    sprintf('<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:%.1fpt;line-height:1.2">%s</div>', g24_size * 20 / 15, title),
    if (!is.null(subtitle)) {
      sprintf(
        '<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:%.1fpt;line-height:1.18;margin-top:1.5pt">%s</div>',
        g24_size * 17 / 15, subtitle
      )
    }
  ))
}

## Notes on their own lines above the source, all in the source gray at the axis-label size.
g24t_source <- function(source, notes = NULL) {
  gt::html(sprintf(
    '<div style="color:%s;line-height:1.33">%s%s</div>', g24t_gray,
    if (is.null(notes)) "" else paste0(notes, "<br>"), source
  ))
}

## A figure boxed in a fill, as the 2024 tables box theirs: a block narrower than its column, the figure inside it.
g24t_box <- function(x, fill, colour = g24t_ink, outline = NA) {
  sprintf(
    paste0(
      '<span style="display:inline-block;min-width:20pt;padding:0.5pt 2pt;text-align:right;background:%s;',
      'color:%s;%s">%s</span>'
    ),
    fill, colour, if (is.na(outline)) "" else sprintf("outline:0.5pt solid %s;outline-offset:-0.5pt;", outline), x
  )
}

## Everything the 2024 tables share: the print ground with no bands, bold column heads over a black rule, a light
## gray rule under every row, the last included, and no rules at the sides.
g24t_table <- function(tbl, id, title, subtitle = NULL, source = NULL, notes = NULL, width = 160) {
  if (!is.null(source)) {
    tbl <- gt::tab_source_note(tbl, g24t_source(source, notes))
  }
  tbl |>
    gt::tab_header(g24t_heading(title, subtitle)) |>
    gt::opt_table_font(font = g24t_font) |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width = paste0(width, "pt"),
      table.align = "left",
      table.background.color = g24t_ground,
      table.font.size = paste0(g24_size, "pt"),
      table.font.color = g24t_ink,
      table.border.top.style = "hidden",
      table.border.bottom.style = "hidden",
      heading.align = "left",
      heading.border.bottom.style = "hidden",
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
      column_labels.border.top.style = "hidden",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = g24t_ink,
      column_labels.border.bottom.width = "0.6pt",
      column_labels.padding = "2pt",
      row_group.font.weight = "bold",
      row_group.background.color = g24t_ground,
      row_group.border.top.style = "hidden",
      row_group.border.bottom.color = g24t_ink,
      row_group.border.bottom.width = "0.6pt",
      table_body.hlines.color = g24t_rule,
      table_body.hlines.width = "0.6pt",
      table_body.border.bottom.color = g24t_rule,
      table_body.border.bottom.width = "0.6pt",
      data_row.padding = "2.5pt",
      source_notes.font.size = paste0(g24_size, "pt"),
      source_notes.border.bottom.style = "hidden",
      source_notes.padding = "4pt"
    ) |>
    gt::opt_css(gsub("ID", id, "
      #ID { display: inline-block; padding: 0 8pt 4pt 8pt !important; background: GROUND; }
      #ID .gt_heading { padding: 0 0 6pt 0 !important; }
      #ID .gt_title, #ID .gt_subtitle { padding: 0 !important; }
      #ID .gt_col_heading, #ID .gt_row, #ID .gt_group_heading, #ID .gt_sourcenote { padding-left: 0 !important; }
      #ID .gt_col_heading { vertical-align: bottom; line-height: 1.15; }
      #ID .gt_row { vertical-align: top; line-height: 1.2; }
      #ID .nowrap { white-space: nowrap; }
      #ID .gt_table_body { border-top: none !important; }
      #ID .gt_col_heading { border-bottom: 0.6pt solid INK !important; }
      #ID .gt_group_heading { border-top: none !important; border-bottom: 0.6pt solid INK !important; }
      #ID .gt_row_group_first td { border-top: 0.6pt solid INK !important; }
    ", fixed = TRUE) |>
      gsub(pattern = "GROUND", replacement = g24t_ground, fixed = TRUE) |>
      gsub(pattern = "INK", replacement = g24t_ink, fixed = TRUE))
}
```

## Tables

Tables sit in a chart's frame: the red tab, headline and bold subtitle on the print ground, the source in gray at the foot.

- **No bands, no vertical rules.** A thin black rule closes the column heads; a thin light gray rule runs under every row, the last included.
- **Heads** are bold, with the unit under the name in regular type.
- **Rows** are all black; a name can be bold, with a description under it in regular black (`20250614_EPC629`).

Web graphics with table-like rows follow the same pattern.

### Standard table

```{r g24-tables-greatest-hits}
g24t_startups <- data.frame(
  company = c("Airbnb", "Dropbox", "Stripe", "Zenefits", "Instacart", "Docker"),
  about = c(
    "Rents out places<br>to stay for local hosts", "File-sharing and<br>storage in the cloud",
    "Software for selling<br>from within apps", "Online HR and<br>payroll services",
    "Grocery collection<br>and delivery service", "Platform to manage<br>distribution of software"
  ),
  value = c(25.5, 10, 5, 4.5, 2, 1.1),
  joined = c(2009, 2007, 2010, 2013, 2012, 2010)
)
g24t_startups$company <- paste0("<b>", g24t_startups$company, "</b><br>", g24t_startups$about)
g24t_startups$about <- NULL

gt::gt(g24t_startups, id = "g24-greatest-hits") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(company) |>
  gt::fmt_number(value, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    company = "Company",
    value = gt::html('Value*<br><span style="font-weight:400">$bn</span>'),
    joined = gt::html('Date of<br>joining')
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", company) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", c(value, joined)) |>
  gt::cols_width(company ~ gt::pct(56), value ~ gt::pct(20), joined ~ gt::pct(24)) |>
  g24t_table(
    "g24-greatest-hits", "Greatest hits", "Largest Y Combinator-funded startups",
    source = "Sources: CB Insights; CrunchBase", notes = "*Latest funding round"
  )
```

```{r g24-tables-divided-by-a-dozen}
g24t_questions <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("Social", "Economic", "Foreign policy"), c(3, 4, 5)),
  question = c(
    "Which comes closest to your position on abortion?",
    "Would you support/oppose a constitutional amendment allowing states to ban gay marriage?",
    "Should gun-control laws be more or less strict than they are now?",
    "Do you support/oppose raising the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour?",
    "What should be done to reduce the federal budget deficit?",
    "Do you support/oppose a single-payer health-care system?",
    "Should our taxes provide free college tuition?",
    "Do you think the US government should be doing more or less in its fight against terrorism?",
    "Do you support/oppose sending ground combat troops to fight IS in Iraq and Syria?",
    "Do you favour/oppose building a wall along the border between the United States and Mexico?",
    "Would you say NAFTA has had a positive/negative effect on the US economy?",
    "Is the government doing enough to combat climate change?"
  )
)
gt::gt(g24t_questions, groupname_col = "group", id = "g24-divided") |>
  gt::tab_options(column_labels.hidden = TRUE) |>
  g24t_table("g24-divided", "Divided by a dozen", "Policy choices in our political proximity model")
```

### With color highlight

Highlight a figure by boxing it, in a block of color narrower than its column.
Set totals in bold with their figures boxed in salmon, keeping red for a single point of focus.

```{r g24-tables-jobs-bill}
g24t_bill <- data.frame(
  item = c(
    "Business tax cuts", "Infrastructure spending, state<br>and local government aid",
    "Unemployment insurance and training", "Payroll-tax cut", "Total", "Paid for by",
    "Limiting deductions for<br>upper-income earners", "Treating carried interest as ordinary income",
    "Limiting oil and gas company tax benefits", "Removing corporate-jet tax breaks", "Total*"
  ),
  bn = c(70, 140, 62, 175, 447, NA, 405, 18, 40, 3, 467)
)
g24t_totals <- which(startsWith(g24t_bill$item, "Total"))
g24t_section <- which(g24t_bill$item == "Paid for by")
g24t_bill$bn <- ifelse(is.na(g24t_bill$bn), "", as.character(g24t_bill$bn))
g24t_bill$bn[g24t_totals] <- g24t_box(g24t_bill$bn[g24t_totals], p24[["salmon"]])

gt::gt(g24t_bill, id = "g24-jobs-bill") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(gt::everything()) |>
  gt::cols_label(item = "New stimulus measures", bn = "$bn") |>
  gt::cols_align("right", bn) |>
  gt::tab_style(gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"), gt::cells_body(rows = g24t_totals)) |>
  ## "Paid for by" heads the second group: bold, over the black rule of a head.
  gt::tab_style(
    list(
      gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      gt::cell_borders(sides = "bottom", color = g24t_ink, weight = "0.6pt")
    ),
    gt::cells_body(rows = g24t_section)
  ) |>
  g24t_table(
    "g24-jobs-bill", "Obama’s jobs bill",
    source = "Source: White House", notes = "*Figures may not sum due to rounding"
  )
```

Fill each figure's box from the sequential red, using the web ramp in print too; the two darkest steps turn their figures white.

```{r g24-tables-strewth}
## Read from the chart.
g24t_strewth <- data.frame(
  rank = c("1", "2", "3=", "3=", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9", "10"),
  country = c("Australia", "Britain", "Canada", "Spain", "United States", "Germany", "France", "Italy", "South Korea",
              "Japan"),
  core = c(3.8, 4.8, 3.0, 3.0, 3.9, 3.1, 2.7, 2.3, 2.5, 2.6),
  expected = c(4.4, 2.4, 4.7, 4.1, 5.3, 2.2, 3.5, 3.3, 2.2, 1.6)
)
## Every other step of the web sequential red, which the chart's fills match.
g24t_heat_steps <- econ$web$sequential_red$value[c(3, 5, 7, 9)]
g24t_heat <- function(x) {
  step <- findInterval(x, c(3, 4, 5)) + 1
  g24t_box(formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1), g24t_heat_steps[step], ifelse(step >= 3, "white", g24t_ink))
}
## The rank in bold, in a column of its own width, before the name.
g24t_strewth$country <- sprintf(
  '<b style="display:inline-block;width:13pt">%s</b>%s', g24t_strewth$rank, g24t_strewth$country
)
g24t_strewth$rank <- NULL
g24t_strewth$core <- g24t_heat(g24t_strewth$core)
g24t_strewth$expected <- g24t_heat(g24t_strewth$expected)

gt::gt(g24t_strewth, id = "g24-strewth") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(gt::everything()) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    country = gt::html('Ranking*<br><span style="font-weight:400">Out of ten<br>countries</span>'),
    core = gt::html(
      'Core prices<sup>†</sup><br><span style="font-weight:400">% increase on<br>a year earlier</span>'
    ),
    expected = gt::html('Inflation<br>expectations<sup>‡</sup><br><span style="font-weight:400">%</span>')
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align("left") |>
  gt::cols_width(country ~ gt::pct(40), core ~ gt::pct(30), expected ~ gt::pct(30)) |>
  g24t_table(
    "g24-strewth", "Strewth", "Selected countries, February 2024 or latest", width = 200,
    source = paste(
      "Sources: OECD; Google; Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland; Morning Consult; Raphael Schoenle; ONS;",
      "<i>The Economist</i>"
    ),
    notes = paste(
      "*Three indicators not shown: Google-search behaviour, inflation dispersion and unit labour costs",
      "<sup>†</sup>Excludes energy and food",
      "<sup>‡</sup>Consumers’ inflation expectations over the next 12 months"
    )
  ) |>
  ## Wider, taller boxes than the totals' above: each about half its column and nearly the height of its row.
  gt::opt_css(paste(
    "#g24-strewth .gt_row { vertical-align: middle !important; }",
    "#g24-strewth .gt_row span { min-width: 30pt !important; padding: 3pt 3pt !important; }"
  ))
```

### Table with one color of box

When color carries no value, box every figure in the single-series red, with white figures and no ramp (`20241214_USC174`).

```{r g24-tables-breakdown}
## Read from the chart `20241214_USC174`.
g24t_breakdown <- data.frame(
  item = c(
    "More administrative insurance costs", "Providers spend more on administrative activities",
    "Higher prescription drug costs", "Physicians earn more", "Registered nurses earn more",
    "More investment in medical machinery/equipment", "Other"
  ),
  share = c("15%", "15%", "10%", "10%", "5%", "<5%", "40%")
)
## One fill for every figure: the print single-series red (measured `#F04F38`), the text white.
g24t_breakdown$share <- g24t_box(g24t_breakdown$share, single24[["print"]], "white")

## The guide's heading with a number box at the right of the headline, as the print charts carry theirs.
g24t_numbered_heading <- function(title, subtitle, number) {
  gt::html(paste0(
    sprintf(
      '<div style="width:%gpt;height:%gpt;background:%s;margin:0 0 %gpt 0"></div>',
      3.4 * g24_size, 0.45 * g24_size, accent24[["print"]], 1.2 * g24_size
    ),
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:%.1fpt;line-height:1.2;display:flex;justify-content:space-between">',
        '<span>%s</span><span style="border:0.8pt solid %s;font-size:%.1fpt;padding:0 3pt;line-height:1.3">%s</span>',
        '</div>'
      ),
      g24_size * 20 / 15, title, g24t_ink, g24_size * 16 / 15, number
    ),
    sprintf(
      '<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:%.1fpt;line-height:1.18;margin-top:1.5pt">%s</div>',
      g24_size * 17 / 15, subtitle
    )
  ))
}

g24t_breakdown_gt <- gt::gt(g24t_breakdown, id = "g24-breakdown") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(gt::everything()) |>
  gt::tab_options(column_labels.hidden = TRUE) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", share) |>
  gt::cols_width(item ~ gt::pct(84), share ~ gt::pct(16)) |>
  g24t_table(
    "g24-breakdown", "Breakdown", source = "Source: The Commonwealth Fund", notes = "*Using 12 comparator countries",
    width = 200
  ) |>
  ## The number box in place of the plain heading, and a thin light gray rule over the first row.
  gt::tab_header(g24t_numbered_heading(
    "Breakdown", "United States, components of excess health spending relative to OECD countries, % estimate*", "2"
  )) |>
  gt::opt_css(paste(
    "#g24-breakdown .gt_row { vertical-align: middle !important; }",
    "#g24-breakdown .gt_row span span { min-width: 16pt !important; padding: 0.3pt 2pt !important; }",
    "#g24-breakdown tbody tr:first-child td { border-top: 0.6pt solid #D1D0C7 !important; }"
  ))
g24t_breakdown_gt
```

### Table with integrated charts

Cells use the charts' marks and colors: single-series red for one measure, red and salmon for a pair keyed by squares in the head, a bar on a light gray track for a share, and a blue or red arrow for a direction (`20250215_FNC938`).

```{r g24-tables-ladder}
## Read from the chart.
g24t_ladder <- data.frame(
  study = c(
    "Peng et al. (2023)", "Brynjolfsson, Li and<br>Raymond (2023)", "Noy and Zhang (2023)",
    "Dell’Acqua et al. (2023)",
    "Chen and Chan (2023)", "Choi, Monahan and<br>Schwarcz (2023)", "Otis et al. (2023)", "Roldan-Mones (2024)",
    "Toner-Rodgers (2024)", "Kim et al. (2024)"
  ),
  topic = c(
    "Coding efficiency", "Customer chat", "Writing quality", "Product design", "Ad effectiveness", "Legal analysis",
    "Profits and revenue", "Debating points", "Material discovery", "Investment decisions"
  ),
  narrows = rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), c(6, 4))
)
## Down in blue where inequality falls, up in red where it rises.
g24t_ladder$inequality <- ifelse(
  g24t_ladder$narrows,
  sprintf('<span style="color:%s;font-weight:600;font-size:1.15em">&darr;</span>', p24[["blue"]]),
  sprintf('<span style="color:%s;font-weight:600;font-size:1.15em">&uarr;</span>', p24[["red"]])
)
g24t_ladder$narrows <- NULL

gt::gt(g24t_ladder, id = "g24-ladder") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(gt::everything()) |>
  gt::cols_label(study = "Study", topic = "Topic", inequality = "Inequality") |>
  gt::cols_align("left", c(study, topic)) |>
  gt::cols_align("center", inequality) |>
  gt::cols_width(study ~ gt::pct(45), topic ~ gt::pct(37), inequality ~ gt::pct(18)) |>
  g24t_table(
    "g24-ladder", "Pulling up the ladder",
    "Impact of generative AI on the gap between<br>high- and low-performing workers",
    source = "Source: <i>The Economist</i>", width = 190
  )
```

```{r g24-tables-what-to-expect}
## Small SVG charts for the cells, in points.
g24t_svg <- function(width, height, body) {
  sprintf(
    '<svg width="%gpt" height="%gpt" viewBox="0 0 %g %g" style="display:block">%s</svg>',
    width, height, width, height, paste(body, collapse = "")
  )
}
g24t_bar <- function(value, max, colour, width = 55, height = 3.5, track = NA) {
  length <- pmax(width * value / max, 0.8)
  g24t_svg(width, height, c(
    if (!is.na(track)) sprintf('<rect width="%g" height="%g" fill="%s"/>', width, height, track),
    sprintf('<rect width="%g" height="%g" fill="%s"/>', length, height, colour)
  ))
}
g24t_dashes <- function(n, colour) {
  if (n == 0) {
    return("")
  }
  g24t_svg(n * 6, 4, sprintf('<rect x="%g" y="1" width="5" height="2.2" fill="%s"/>', (seq_len(n) - 1) * 6, colour))
}
g24t_dots <- function(n, colour, per_row = 10) {
  i <- seq_len(n) - 1
  g24t_svg(per_row * 3.6, ceiling(n / per_row) * 3.6, sprintf(
    '<circle cx="%g" cy="%g" r="1.35" fill="%s"/>',
    1.8 + (i %% per_row) * 3.6, 1.8 + (i %/% per_row) * 3.6, colour
  ))
}
g24t_square <- function(colour) {
  sprintf('<span style="display:inline-block;width:5pt;height:5pt;background:%s;margin-right:2pt"></span>', colour)
}
g24t_mark <- function(x, mark) paste0(x, ifelse(mark == "", "", paste0("<sup>", mark, "</sup>")))

g24t_one <- single24[["print"]]
g24t_applied_col <- p24[["red"]]
g24t_decided_col <- p24[["salmon"]]

g24t_asylum <- data.frame(
  country = c("Germany", "Sweden", "Hungary", "Britain", "United<br>States", "Australia"),
  applications = c(173070, 75090, 41370, 31260, 121160, 8960),
  decisions = c(97415, 40015, 5445, 26055, 71765, 13198),
  decisions_mark = c("", "", "", "", "†", "†"),
  accepted = c(42, 77, 9, 39, 30, 19),
  accepted_mark = c("", "", "", "", "†", "†"),
  wait = c("3 months", "Immediately", "9 months", "12 months", "6 months", ""),
  wait_months = c(3, 0, 9, 12, 6, 0),
  wait_note = c(
    "", "Without restrictions", "Working only in a<br>reception centre",
    "Only jobs where gov’t sees a<br>shortage (medics, engineers)",
    "In practice, 92% of<br>applicants wait longer", "Most applicants cannot<br>work as they are in detention"
  ),
  benefits = c(374, 226, 86, 217, 0, 275),
  benefits_note = c("", "", "Maximum", "", "", "")
)
g24t_origins <- list(
  c("Syria" = 23, "Serbia / Kosovo" = 14, "Eritrea" = 8),
  c("Syria" = 40, "Stateless" = 10, "Eritrea" = 8),
  c("Serbia / Kosovo" = 51, "Afghanistan" = 21, "Syria" = 16),
  c("Eritrea" = 13, "Pakistan" = 11, "Syria" = 8),
  c("Mexico" = 12, "China" = 11, "El Salvador" = 8),
  c("China" = 19, "India" = 13, "Pakistan" = 10)
)
g24t_origin_mark <- c("", "", "", "", "", "‡")
g24t_top <- max(g24t_asylum$applications)

g24t_cells <- data.frame(
  country = paste0("<b>", g24t_asylum$country, "</b>"),
  applied = paste0(
    format(g24t_asylum$applications, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
    vapply(g24t_asylum$applications, g24t_bar, "", max = g24t_top, colour = g24t_applied_col),
    '<div style="height:1.5pt"></div>',
    vapply(g24t_asylum$decisions, g24t_bar, "", max = g24t_top, colour = g24t_decided_col),
    g24t_mark(format(g24t_asylum$decisions, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), g24t_asylum$decisions_mark)
  ),
  origin = vapply(seq_along(g24t_origins), function(i) {
    o <- g24t_origins[[i]]
    paste0(
      sprintf('<div class="nowrap">%s</div>', g24t_mark(paste(names(o), o), g24t_origin_mark[i])),
      vapply(o, g24t_bar, "", max = 51, colour = g24t_one, height = 2.5),
      collapse = ""
    )
  }, ""),
  accepted = paste0(
    g24t_mark(g24t_asylum$accepted, g24t_asylum$accepted_mark),
    vapply(g24t_asylum$accepted, g24t_bar, "", max = 100, colour = g24t_one, width = 28, track = g24t_rule)
  ),
  wait = paste0(
    ifelse(g24t_asylum$wait == "", "", sprintf("<b>%s</b>", g24t_asylum$wait)),
    vapply(g24t_asylum$wait_months, g24t_dashes, "", colour = g24t_one),
    sprintf('<div class="nowrap">%s</div>', g24t_asylum$wait_note)
  ),
  benefits = ifelse(
    g24t_asylum$benefits == 0,
    "<i>Nil</i>",
    paste0(
      '<div style="display:flex;gap:2pt;align-items:flex-start">',
      paste0("€", g24t_asylum$benefits),
      vapply(round(g24t_asylum$benefits / 10), g24t_dots, "", colour = g24t_one),
      "</div>",
      ifelse(g24t_asylum$benefits_note == "", "", paste0("<i>", g24t_asylum$benefits_note, "</i>"))
    )
  )
)

gt::gt(g24t_cells, id = "g24-what-to-expect") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(gt::everything()) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    country = "Country",
    applied = gt::html(paste0(
      '<span class="nowrap">', g24t_square(g24t_applied_col), "Applications*</span><br>",
      '<span class="nowrap">', g24t_square(g24t_decided_col), "Decisions made</span>"
    )),
    origin = gt::html('Mainly from<br><span style="font-weight:400">%</span>'),
    accepted = gt::html('Accepted<br><span style="font-weight:400">%</span>'),
    wait = gt::html("Minimum wait before<br>permitted to work"),
    benefits = gt::html("State benefits<br>per month")
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align("left") |>
  gt::cols_width(
    country ~ "34pt", applied ~ "60pt", origin ~ "62pt", accepted ~ "34pt", wait ~ "88pt", benefits ~ "54pt"
  ) |>
  g24t_table(
    "g24-what-to-expect", "What to expect", "Asylum processes, selected countries, 2014",
    source = "Sources: UNHCR; government statistics; <i>The Economist</i>",
    notes = "*From UNHCR 2014 report &nbsp;†From UNHCR Statistical Database &nbsp;‡2012-13 figures",
    width = 332
  )
```

### Indicator tables

The weekly indicator tables keep the [2018 format](economist-2017-styleguide.html#indicator-tables) and change only color and typeface:

- **No bands.** A thin London 70 rule (`#B3B3B3`) runs under every row.
- **Gray structure.** A London 40 rule (`#666666`) closes the column heads, separates the six country groups and closes the table, as does the vertical rule before each column group.
- **Gray key boxes.** The latest figure is boxed in London 85 (`#D9D9D9`), or in salmon (the print salmon at 75%) where negative; there is no blue.
- **As in 2018.** No signs on positive figures, periods in a column of their own in smaller type, group names flush left in bold over the unit, light labels.
- **A narrower typeface.**

```{r g24-tables-indicators}
source("economist-indicators.R")
## The 2024 style: no bands, a London 70 rule under every row and London 40 rules between the groups, and the latest
## figures boxed in London 85 or, where negative, in salmon.
indicator_table("2024")
```

## Double-scale charts

Double scales are rare; a column-and-line chart usually puts the line on the columns' own scale.
A chart that does need two scales (`20260829_FNC018`):

- **Two colors.** Red for the series in focus, gray for the other.
- **Colored axes.** Each axis's labels take its series' color; the axes share the gridlines.
- **Titles** above the axes, in the series' colors and the weight of a subtitle, the left ranged left and the right ranged right.
- **Broken scales** get a small zigzag at the foot.

### One line on each axis

```{r g24-tables-out-of-steam, econ_height = 175}
## Series in pixel coordinates, converted to years and values.
g24t_px_year <- function(x) 1955 + (x - 115) / 8
g24t_px_value <- function(y) (633 - y) / 5.27
g24t_rail <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    series = "track",
    year = g24t_px_year(c(115, 140, 155, 172, 190, 205, 220, 240, 300, 420, 430, 450, 470, 500, 520, 588)),
    value = g24t_px_value(c(508, 509, 511, 520, 535, 548, 553, 557, 558, 558, 553, 553, 553, 553, 557, 556))
  ),
  data.frame(
    series = "passengers",
    year = g24t_px_year(c(
      115, 131, 148, 160, 172, 190, 205, 220, 237, 250, 262, 272, 285, 298, 312, 322, 333, 340, 353, 365, 378,
      395, 410, 428, 440, 455, 470, 480, 490, 505, 520, 535, 548, 560, 575, 588
    )),
    value = g24t_px_value(c(
      458, 442, 445, 452, 465, 467, 478, 482, 472, 485, 475, 470, 483, 475, 465, 478, 490, 480, 478, 470, 457,
      460, 468, 480, 465, 450, 430, 428, 420, 412, 390, 370, 360, 335, 318, 302
    ))
  )
)

## The two series of a double-scale chart: red for the focus, dark gray for the other.
g24t_focus <- p24[["red"]]
g24t_other_series <- p24[["dark gray"]]

## Both value axes, each above its gridlines, and each axis's labels and title in its series' color.
g24t_two_axes <- function(left, right) {
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = left, hjust = 0),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = right, hjust = 1),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = left, face = "bold", size = rel(17 / 15), hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = right, face = "bold", size = rel(17 / 15), hjust = 1)
  )
}

g24t_steam <- ggplot(g24t_rail, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  ## An event: a thin gray rule with its label above it.
  annotate("segment", x = 1994, xend = 1994, y = 0, yend = 64, linewidth = g24_lw(0.5), colour = g24t_gray) +
  annotate("text", x = 1994, y = 66, label = "Privatisation begins", size = g24_pt(6.5), colour = g24t_gray,
           vjust = 0) +
  geom_line(linewidth = g24_lw(1.5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(track = g24t_other_series, passengers = g24t_focus), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "National rail track\n'000 km", limits = c(0, 70), breaks = seq(0, 70, 10), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~., name = "Passenger kilometres\nbn", breaks = seq(0, 70, 10), guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1955, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2014),
    labels = c("1955", "70", "80", "90", "2000", "14"), limits = c(1945, 2022), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Out of steam", subtitle = "Britain, railways", x = NULL, caption = "Source: Department for Transport") +
  g24_theme() +
  g24t_two_axes(g24t_other_series, g24t_focus)

g24_chart(g24t_steam)
```

### Three lines on the left-hand axis

```{r g24-tables-golden-triangle, econ_height = 165}

g24t_golden <- ggplot(g24t_nafta, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = g24_lw(1.5)) +
  geom_text(data = g24t_nafta_labels, aes(label = .data$series, hjust = .data$hjust), size = g24_text,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
```

### Line and column

Use blue columns, the main contrast to red, as salmon is too pale for axis labels.

```{r g24-tables-chavismo, econ_height = 175}
g24t_venezuela <- data.frame(
  year = 2004:2016,
  gdp = c(18.3, 10.3, 9.9, 8.8, 5.3, -3.2, -1.5, 4.2, 5.6, 1.3, -3.9, -5.7, -18.6),
  prices = c(22, 16, 14, 19, 31, 27, 29, 26, 21, 41, 70, 180, 800)
)

g24t_chavismo <- ggplot(g24t_venezuela, aes(.data$year)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = .data$gdp), fill = p24[["blue"]], width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = g24t_ink, linewidth = g24_lw(1)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = .data$prices * 20 / 800), colour = g24t_focus, linewidth = g24_lw(1.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "GDP", limits = c(-20, 20), breaks = seq(-20, 20, 5), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . * 800 / 20, name = "Consumer prices,\nyear-end", breaks = seq(-800, 800, 200),
      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2004, 2016, 2), labels = c("2004", "06", "08", "10", "12", "14", "16*"),

  ) +

    title = "Chavismo in action", subtitle = "Venezuela, % change on a year earlier", x = NULL,
    caption = "*Preliminary estimate\nSources: IMF; Reuters"

g24_chart(g24t_chavismo)
```

### What to avoid

Mark a broken scale with a zigzag and an inverted one in its title; the faults the 2017 guide warns of remain.

```{r g24-tables-double-scale-avoid, econ_height = 155}
## A zigzag where a scale is broken, centred on `x`, `y`, `w` data units wide and `h` high.
g24t_break <- function(x, y, w, h, colour = g24t_ink) {
  annotate(
    "path", x = x + w * c(-0.5, -0.15, -0.05, 0.05, 0.15, 0.5), y = y + h * c(0, 0, 0.5, -0.5, 0, 0),
    colour = colour, linewidth = g24_lw(0.6)
  )
}

g24t_px_euro <- function(y) 1 + (473 - y) / 660
g24t_months <- 2013.5 + (0:23) / 12
g24t_qe <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "Euro", year = g24t_months, value = g24t_px_euro(c(
    247, 245, 234, 236, 243, 250, 255, 268, 294, 310, 322, 333, 380, 397, 432, 432, 408, 405, 420, 411, 404, 404,
    438, 428
  ))),
  data.frame(series = "Italy", year = g24t_months, value = g24t_px_euro(c(
    284, 305, 324, 332, 344, 351, 367, 372, 392, 400, 392, 420, 430, 445, 465, 468, 450, 418, 402, 435, 420, 433,
    441, 458
  ))),
  data.frame(series = "Euro area", year = g24t_months[1:23], value = g24t_px_euro(c(
    337, 346, 358, 376, 380, 398, 406, 418, 427, 438, 442, 455, 465, 468, 486, 491, 458, 440, 450, 457, 450, 468,
    472
  )))
)
g24t_qe_cols <- c(Euro = g24t_focus, Italy = p24[["blue"]], `Euro area` = p24[["light blue"]])

## The euro's scale starts at 0.9, not zero: the panel runs below the lowest gridline to make room for the zigzag.
g24t_quantifying <- ggplot(g24t_qe, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = g24_lw(1.5)) +
  annotate("text", x = 2014.0, y = 1.24, label = "Italy", colour = p24[["blue"]], size = g24_text) +
  annotate("text", x = 2014.05, y = 1.03, label = "Euro area", colour = p24[["light blue"]], size = g24_text) +
  g24t_break(2013.19 + 0.08, 0.875, 0.16, 0.016) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24t_qe_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "Euro against the\ndollar, $ per €", limits = c(0.85, 1.4001), breaks = seq(0.9, 1.4, 0.1),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ (. - 0.9) * 10, name = "Ten-year government-\nbond yields, %", breaks = 0:5,
      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2014, 2015), labels = c("2014", "2015"), limits = c(2013.19, 2015.69),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "Quantifying QE", x = NULL, caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters") +
  g24_theme() +
  g24t_two_axes(g24t_focus, g24t_ink)

g24_chart(g24t_quantifying)
```

```{r g24-tables-double-scale-avoid-2, econ_height = 155}
g24t_beneath <- data.frame(
  year = 2002:2015,
  cash = c(27, 68, 75, 98, 79, 90, 91, -5, 32, 31, 18, -30, 1, -50)
)
g24t_brent_x <- c(100, 130, 165, 190, 205, 225, 237, 258, 275, 285, 295, 302, 310, 318, 324, 340, 358, 375, 385, 395,
                  405, 418, 430, 440, 455, 470, 485, 500, 510, 520, 530, 540, 550, 560, 575, 590)

                  345, 340, 320, 345, 335, 345, 340, 340, 345, 400, 440, 430, 455, 480, 460, 450)
g24t_brent <- data.frame(year = 2002 + (g24t_brent_x - 100) / 33.7, price = (538 - g24t_brent_y) / 1.88)

## The right-hand scale is the left shifted by 60, so the two zero lines do not coincide.
g24t_lies <- ggplot() +

  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = g24t_ink, linewidth = g24_lw(1)) +

      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()

    breaks = seq(2002, 2016, 2), labels = c("2002", "04", "06", "08", "10", "12", "14", "16"),
    limits = c(2000.1, 2018.3), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "What lies beneath", x = NULL, caption = "Source: BCG") +
  g24_theme() +
  g24t_two_axes(p24[["blue"]], g24t_focus)

g24_chart(g24t_lies)
```

```{r g24-tables-double-scale-avoid-3, econ_height = 165}
g24t_rand_x <- c(88, 95, 110, 125, 133, 140, 150, 160, 172, 185, 200, 215, 228, 240, 255, 270, 285, 300, 315, 330, 345,
                 360, 375, 390, 405, 420, 435, 450, 465, 480, 495, 510, 520, 530, 540, 550, 560, 575, 582)
g24t_rand_y <- c(258, 290, 290, 300, 375, 340, 360, 300, 290, 272, 275, 270, 265, 258, 262, 252, 262, 285, 282, 320, 310,
                 325, 330, 345, 350, 375, 380, 385, 370, 395, 420, 470, 520, 550, 490, 470, 480, 460, 480)
g24t_sacci_x <- c(88, 110, 125, 140, 150, 160, 172, 180, 200, 210, 225, 237, 250, 262, 272, 285, 300, 315, 330, 345,
                  360, 375, 385, 395, 410, 420, 435, 445, 460, 475, 485, 500, 515, 525, 535, 545, 555, 570, 580)
g24t_sacci_y <- c(285, 295, 330, 300, 350, 330, 290, 300, 300, 290, 240, 235, 255, 230, 245, 270, 280, 285, 350, 330,
                  340, 370, 365, 355, 350, 365, 348, 340, 360, 385, 345, 395, 410, 470, 490, 480, 455, 470, 475)
g24t_zuma <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "rand", year = 2008 + (g24t_rand_x - 88) / 55, value = 6 + (g24t_rand_y - 228) / 30),
  data.frame(series = "sacci", year = 2008 + (g24t_sacci_x - 88) / 55, value = 6 + (g24t_sacci_y - 228) / 30)
)

## An index against an inverted currency scale: two disparate measures forced into visual correlation. The
## inversion is stated in the scale's title, and neither scale starts at zero.
g24t_zuma_plot <- ggplot(g24t_zuma, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = g24_lw(1.5)) +
  g24t_break(2007.04 + 0.3, 18.5, 0.6, 0.45, colour = g24t_focus) +
  g24t_break(2018.2 - 0.3, 18.5, 0.6, 0.45, colour = g24t_other_series) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(rand = g24t_focus, sacci = g24t_other_series), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_reverse(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "Rand per $,\ninverted scale", limits = c(19, 6), breaks = seq(6, 18, 3), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ 120 - (. - 6) * 40 / 12, name = "SACCI Business\nConfidence Index,\n2015=100", breaks = seq(80, 120, 10),
      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 2008.5 + 0:8, labels = c("2008", sprintf("%02d", 9:16)), limits = c(2007.04, 2018.2), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "The Zuma years", subtitle = "South Africa", x = NULL,
       caption = "Sources: Thomson Reuters; SACCI") +
  g24_theme() +
  g24t_two_axes(g24t_focus, g24t_other_series)

g24_chart(g24t_zuma_plot)
```

## Blob heads

Blob heads are bubbles sized by value, in the print light gray (`20250531_WBC482`):

- **A column of bubbles**, one to a row, sized by area, at the right of the bars.
- **The figure** in black, centred on its bubble or beside it (see [below](#bubbles-and-numbers-outside-the-bar)).
- **A callout** with the unit and a pointer turned down at the bubbles names the column.
- **Missing values** are "nil" in italics.

### Numbers inside the bubbles

```{r g24-tables-big-mac, econ_height = 335}
g24t_bigmac <- data.frame(
  country = c("Switzerland", "Norway", "Sweden", "Brazil", "United States", "Euro area", "Britain", "Japan", "Turkey",
              "China", "Vietnam", "India", "Mexico", "Russia"),
  y2016 = c(31, 6, 5, -32, -1, -19, -14, -37, -31, -46, -48, -61, -43, -68),
  y2017 = c(27, 14, 4, 2, 0, -19, -24, -35, -41, -43, -45, -50, -54, -57),
  price = c(6.4, 5.8, 5.3, 5.1, 5.1, 4.1, 3.8, 3.3, 3.0, 2.8, 2.6, 2.5, 2.3, 2.2)
)
g24t_bigmac$country <- factor(g24t_bigmac$country, levels = rev(g24t_bigmac$country))
g24t_bigmac_long <- data.frame(
  country = rep(g24t_bigmac$country, 2),
  year = rep(c("January 2016", "January 2017"), each = nrow(g24t_bigmac)),
  value = c(g24t_bigmac$y2016, g24t_bigmac$y2017)
)
## The bubbles: the print light gray, sized by area.
g24t_blob <- p24[["light gray"]]

## Footnote marks hang off the country names as superscripts.
g24t_bigmac_marks <- c("United States" = "†", "Euro area" = "‡", "China" = "§", "India" = "**")
g24t_bigmac_labels <- function(x) {
  parse(text = ifelse(
    x %in% names(g24t_bigmac_marks), paste0("'", x, "'^'", g24t_bigmac_marks[x], "'"), paste0("'", x, "'")
  ))
}

g24t_big_mac <- ggplot(g24t_bigmac, aes(y = .data$country)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = g24t_ink, linewidth = g24_lw(1)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = .data$y2016, xend = .data$y2017, yend = .data$country), colour = p24[["dark gray"]],
               linewidth = g24_lw(1.5)) +
  geom_point(data = g24t_bigmac_long, aes(x = .data$value, colour = .data$year), size = 2.2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 66, size = .data$price), colour = g24t_blob, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 66, label = format(.data$price, nsmall = 1)), size = g24_text) +
  ## The callout over the column, its pointer turned down at the bubbles.
  annotate("label_economist_2017", x = 66, y = 15.1, label = "Big Mac price*, $", pointer = "bottom",
           fill = g24t_blob, hjust = 0.9,
           family = economist_2017_font(), size = g24_text) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6.5) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-80, 75), ylim = c(0.5, 14.5), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", breaks = seq(-80, 40, 20), labels = c("-80", "", "-40", "", "0", "", "40")) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = g24t_bigmac_labels) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("January 2016" = p24[["salmon"]], "January 2017" = p24[["red"]])) +
  labs(
    title = "The Big Mac index",
    subtitle = "Local currency under (-) / over (+)\nvaluation against the dollar, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "*At market exchange rates (Jan 11th 2017)\n†Average of four cities\n‡Weighted average of member countries\n",
      "§Average of five cities **Maharaja Mac\nSources: McDonald's; The Economist"
    )
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  theme(
    axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    legend.margin = margin(b = 14)
  )

g24_chart(g24t_big_mac)
```

### Bubbles and numbers outside the bar

Centre the figures on the bubbles.

```{r g24-tables-up-in-air, econ_height = 254}
g24t_travel <- data.frame(
  country = c("China", "India", "Germany", "Spain", "United States", "Britain", "South Korea", "Canada", "Brazil",
              "France", "Italy", "Australia", "Japan", "Netherlands", "Russia"),
  change = c(16.5, 9.7, 7.6, 6.7, 5.4, 5.4, 3.9, 3.8, 3.7, 2.0, 1.3, 1.3, 1.1, -1.7, -6.6),
  bn = c(261, 26, 58, 18, 288, 44, 32, 23, 32, 36, 31, 21, 62, 18, 21)
)
g24t_travel$country <- factor(g24t_travel$country, levels = rev(g24t_travel$country))

g24t_air <- ggplot(g24t_travel, aes(.data$country, .data$change)) +
  geom_col(fill = single24[["print"]], width = 0.65) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = g24t_ink, linewidth = g24_lw(1)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = 25.5, size = .data$bn), colour = g24t_blob, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 25.5, label = .data$bn), size = g24_text) +
  annotate("label_economist_2017", x = 15.85, y = 25.5, label = "$bn", pointer = "bottom", fill = g24t_blob,
           family = economist_2017_font(), size = g24_text) +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.45, 15.5), ylim = c(-10.5, 30), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", breaks = seq(-10, 15, 5), labels = c("-10", "", "0", "5", "10", "15")) +
  labs(
    title = "Up in the air",
    subtitle = "Business travel spending, 2014\n% change on a year earlier",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: GBTA"
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

g24_chart(g24t_air)
```

Or set the figures beside the bubbles, ranged left in a column of their own.

```{r g24-tables-believers, econ_height = 175}
## Read from the chart.
g24t_catholics <- data.frame(
  region = factor(
    c("Africa", "Oceania", "Asia", "Americas", "Europe"),
    levels = rev(c("Africa", "Oceania", "Asia", "Americas", "Europe"))
  ),
  change = c(22.3, 16.6, 12.9, 8.6, -0.6),
  m = c(272, 11, 154, 666, 286)
)

g24t_believers <- ggplot(g24t_catholics, aes(.data$region, .data$change)) +
  geom_col(fill = single24[["print"]], width = 0.62) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = g24t_ink, linewidth = g24_lw(1)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = 31, size = .data$m), colour = g24t_blob, show.legend = FALSE) +
  ## The figures beside the bubbles, ranged left.
  geom_text(aes(y = 37, label = .data$m), hjust = 0, size = g24_text) +
  annotate("label_economist_2017", x = 1, y = 27.8, label = "2022, m", pointer = "right", hjust = 1,
           fill = g24t_blob, family = economist_2017_font(), size = g24_text) +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.45, 5.55), ylim = c(-7, 41.5), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", breaks = seq(-5, 25, 5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Believers",
    subtitle = "Catholic population, 2013-22, % change",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: The Vatican"
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

g24_chart(g24t_believers)
```

### Equal-sized number blocks

Equal-sized blocks are light gray, with the callout beside the last.

```{r g24-tables-starting-small, econ_height = 175}
g24t_exchanges <- data.frame(
  exchange = rep(c("Johannesburg", "Nigeria", "Mauritius", "Nairobi", "Namibia", "BRVM*"), 2),
  listing = rep(c("Domestic", "Foreign"), each = 6),
  listed = c(306, 176, 75, 65, 8, 41, 71, 0, 0, 0, 33, 0)
)
g24t_exchanges$exchange <- factor(g24t_exchanges$exchange, levels = rev(unique(g24t_exchanges$exchange)))
g24t_exchanges$listing <- factor(g24t_exchanges$listing, levels = c("Foreign", "Domestic"))
g24t_caps <- data.frame(
  exchange = factor(levels(g24t_exchanges$exchange), levels = levels(g24t_exchanges$exchange)),
  cap = c(11.6, 2.3, 19.9, 6.2, 29.3, 943)
)

g24t_small <- ggplot(g24t_exchanges, aes(.data$exchange, .data$listed)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = .data$listing), width = 0.65) +
  geom_tile(data = g24t_caps, aes(y = 505, height = 70), width = 0.6, fill = g24t_blob) +
  geom_text(data = g24t_caps, aes(y = 505, label = .data$cap), size = g24_text) +
  annotate("label_economist_2017", x = 1, y = 462, label = "Market cap, $bn", pointer = "right", fill = g24t_blob,
           family = economist_2017_font(), size = g24_text) +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.45, 6.55), ylim = c(0, 548), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Domestic = p24[["red"]], Foreign = p24[["salmon"]]), limits = c("Domestic", "Foreign")) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", breaks = seq(0, 400, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "Starting small",
    subtitle = "Number of companies listed on stock\nexchanges, October 2016",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "*West African regional exchange\nSource: World Federation of Exchanges"
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

g24_chart(g24t_small)
```

### Text blocks

Text blocks are black type on the print light gray in a box with a pointer, as in 2017, but rare: most annotations are labels on thin black leader lines (`20240720_ASC360`).
`geom_label_economist_2017()` draws the boxes.

```{r g24-tables-text-blocks, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 95}
g24t_blocks <- data.frame(
  x = c(0.9, 2.2, 1.6, 2.6, 3),
  y = c(1.9, 1.6, 0.7, 1, 2),
  label = c("ECB announces QE", "ECB announces\nQE beginning", "ECB announces QE", "ECB announces QE",
            "ECB announces QE"),
  pointer = c("bottom", "bottom", "right", "top", "left"),
  hjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.15, 0.5)
)
ggplot(g24t_blocks, aes(.data$x, .data$y)) +
  ## One layer per pointer side; x and y are where each pointer touches.
  lapply(split(g24t_blocks, g24t_blocks$pointer), function(d) {
    geom_label_economist_2017(aes(label = .data$label, hjust = .data$hjust), data = d, pointer = d$pointer[1],
                              fill = g24t_blob, family = economist_2017_font(), size = g24_text)
  }) +
  geom_point(colour = accent24[["print"]], size = 0.6) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.4, 4.4), ylim = c(-0.2, 3), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  g24_theme() +
  g24_no_axes()
```
